parsed.why: Dead-letter colonial statute, no prosecutions documented, no government abuses, UN SOGI-support signatory, third-gender community recognised in HIV response; latent felony exposure plus thin data holds it a step below full acceptance.

State actively targets trans identity: propaganda/pornography laws criminalising trans depiction, mass detentions with custody abuse, police beatings and data collection, official demonisation, no recourse or hate-crime redress.

No criminalisation but documented tier-1 exposures: custody by birth sex, strip-searches by birth sex, ward bans (Joelle death), single-sex code in force, functioning institutions enforcing hostile policy outweigh strong general tolerance.

No criminalisation; hate-crime law covering gender identity and anti-discrimination statute, UN expert visit with good practices; but weak enforcement, ten logged trans violence cases, social disapproval place it mid-band.

Enforced criminalisation applied to foreigners (deportations, arrests), detention in abusive facilities, authoritarian state labelling 'gay' as slur, no protections, conversion therapy; enforcement documented though dated, structural hostility current.
